calls.reason: SoftBank's October disclosure says all bridge borrowings were repaid and unused capacity canceled while OpenAI remained private. That substantially undermines the claimed dependence on an IPO to avoid a liquidity crisis.
ARC Prize reports substantial generalization gains but explicitly says they do not establish AGI. Neither those results nor the absence of AGI settles the unlimited forecast.

Reuters and Anthropic's filing support the revenue figures. Ramp reports rising spending in a selected group, while Tom's Hardware describes cost cutting; neither establishes the claimed broad retreat or its cause.

DeepSeek supplies hypothetical economics, while Bloomberg reports positive OpenAI compute margins. These measure different things, leaving the subjective claim about compelling profitability evidence unclear.
Sherlund documents an October selloff, not a clear collapse of the AI boom. Microsoft's strong results cover an earlier quarter and cannot establish how most big tech fares afterward.
The 2030 demand deadline remains ahead. J.P. Morgan's capital expenditure projection establishes neither realized compute demand nor the predicted industry losses.
